title: The Foundation (Tawheed)
summary: Islam is not a new religion but the primordial faith of submission to the One True God (Allāh), revived through the final Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The essence of this submission is Tawheed the absolute Oneness of God in His Lordship, His Names and Attributes, and His right to be worshipped alone.

overview.heading: Tawheed: Absolute Oneness
overview.content:
Tawheed means declaring Allah's absolute oneness in all aspects. Qur'anic "Say: He is Allah, the One." (Al Ikhlas 112:1) Reference: "Kitab al Tawheed" by Ibn Khuzaymah.

References:
Quran Al-Ikhlāṣ 112:1; Kitab al Tawheed by Ibn Khuzaymah; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The right of Allah upon His servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him)

overview.heading: Tawheed Has Three Essential Categories
overview.content:
It has three essential categories that cannot be separated: Tawheed al Rububiyyah (Lordship), Tawheed al Asma wa al Sifat (Names and Attributes), and Tawheed al 'Ibadah (Worship). Reference: "Al Qawa'id al Arba'" by Muhammad ibn 'Abd al Wahhab.

References:
Al Qawa'id al Arba' by Muhammad ibn 'Abd al Wahhab; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise)

overview.heading: Tawheed al Rububiyyah (Lordship)
overview.content:
Oneness in Lordship: Allah alone creates, provides, and controls. Qur'anic "Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is Disposer of all affairs." (Az Zumar 39:62) Reference: "Al Qawa'id al Arba'" by Muhammad ibn 'Abd al Wahhab.

References:
Quran Az-Zumar 39:62; Al Qawa'id al Arba' by Muhammad ibn 'Abd al Wahhab; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The right of Allah upon His servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him)

overview.heading: Tawheed al Asma wa al Sifat (Names and Attributes)
overview.content:
Oneness in Names and Attributes as revealed, without distortion. Qur'anic "There is nothing like unto Him..." (Ash Shura 42:11) Reference: "Al 'Aqidah al Wasitiyyah" by Ibn Taymiyyah.

References:
Quran Ash-Shūrā 42:11; Al 'Aqidah al Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever learns them will enter Paradise)

overview.heading: Tawheed al 'Ibadah (Worship)
overview.content:
Oneness in worship: directing all acts to Allah alone. Qur'anic "Worship Allah and associate none with Him..." (An Nisa' 4:36) Reference: "Kashf al Shubuhat" by Muhammad ibn 'Abd al Wahhab.

References:
Quran An-Nisāʾ 4:36; Kashf al Shubuhat by Muhammad ibn 'Abd al Wahhab; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The most beloved deeds to Allah are those done regularly, even if small)

overview.heading: Iman: Six Pillars of Faith
overview.content:
Iman has six pillars including belief in Allah and the Last Day. "It is to believe in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and Divine Decree..." (Sahih Muslim 8a) Reference: "Sharh Usul al Iman" by Ibn 'Uthaymin.

References:
Hadith: Sahih Muslim 8a (Hadith Jibril); Sharh Usul al Iman by Ibn 'Uthaymin

overview.heading: Ihsan: Worship as if You See Him
overview.content:
Ihsan is worshipping Allah as if you see Him, knowing He sees you. "To worship Allah as if you see Him..." (Sahih al Bukhari 50) Reference: "Ihya' 'Ulum al Din" by Al Ghazali.

References:
Hadith: Sahih al Bukhari 50 (Hadith Jibril); Ihya' 'Ulum al Din by Al Ghazali

overview.heading: Shirk: Associating Partners with Allah
overview.content:
Shirk is associating partners with Allah and is the only unforgivable sin if unrepented. "Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him..." (An Nisa' 4:48) Reference: "Al Sawa'iq al Mursalah" by Ibn al Qayyim.

References:
Quran An-Nisāʾ 4:48; Al Sawa'iq al Mursalah by Ibn al Qayyim; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (Whoever meets Allah associating anything with Him will enter the Fire)

overview.heading: Shahadah Conditions
overview.content:
The Shahadah ("La ilaha illallah") has seven conditions for validity derived from the Qur'an and Sunnah: knowledge, certainty, acceptance, and more. Reference: "Sharh Usul al Iman" by Ibn Baz, p. 45.

References:
Sharh Usul al Iman by Ibn Baz, p. 45; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Whoever says La ilaha illallah sincerely from his heart will enter Paradise)

overview.heading: Tawheed Message of All Prophets
overview.content:
Tawheed was the first message of all Prophets from Nuh to Muhammad ﷺ. "We sent every Messenger with the revelation: 'Worship Allah and avoid false gods...'" (An Nahl 16:36) Reference: "Tariq al Hijratayn" by Ibn al Qayyim.

References:
Quran An-Naḥl 16:36; Tariq al Hijratayn by Ibn al Qayyim; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The prophets are brothers; their religion is one)

overview.heading: Rejecting Tawheed Nullifies Deeds
overview.content:
Rejecting Tawheed invalidates deeds regardless of outward form. "If they had associated others with Allah, all they did would have been nullified." (Al An'am 6:88) Reference: "Majmu' al Fatawa" by Ibn Taymiyyah, vol. 1, p. 98.

References:
Quran Al-Anʿām 6:88; Majmu' al Fatawa by Ibn Taymiyyah, vol. 1, p. 98; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (Whoever meets Allah associating anything with Him will enter the Fire)

title: The Beliefs: The Six Pillars of Iman
summary: The Islamic creed (ʿAqīdah) is built upon six fundamental articles of faith (Arkān al-Īmān). These beliefs form the foundation of a Muslim’s worldview and are derived from the definitive texts of the Qur’ān and the authentic Sunnah.

overview.heading: Belief in Allāh (Allāh سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى)
overview.content:
To affirm Allāh’s Oneness (Tawḥīd) in His Lordship, His Names and Attributes, and His right to worship, as described in the Qur’ān and Sunnah without distortion. Key "Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence." (Āli ʿImrān 3:2) Resource: Kitāb al-Tawḥīd by Shaykh al-Islām Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb.

References:
Quran Āl ʿImrān 3:2; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The right of Allah upon His servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him)

overview.heading: Belief in the Angels (Al-Malāʾikah)
overview.content:
To believe in the angels as honored servants of Allāh, created from light, who never disobey Him and execute His commands precisely. Key "The Messenger believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. All believe in Allāh, His angels, His books, and His messengers..." (Al-Baqarah 2:285) Resource: Badʾ al-Khalq (Chapter on Creation) in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:285; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (The angels were created from light)

overview.heading: Belief in the Revealed Books (Al-Kutub)
overview.content:
To believe that Allāh revealed divine scriptures to His messengers as guidance, including the Qur’ān (the final, preserved book), the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms. Key "And We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture..." (Al-Māʾidah 5:48) Resource: Al-ʿAqīdah al-Ṭaḥāwiyyah (Articles 7-8).

References:
Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:48; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (I left among you the Book of Allah)

overview.heading: Belief in the Messengers (Al-Rusul)
overview.content:
To believe that Allāh sent prophets and messengers to every nation, beginning with Ādam and ending with Muḥammad ﷺ, all calling to Tawḥīd. We believe in all of them without distinction. Key "And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], 'Worship Allāh and avoid false deities...'" (Al-Naḥl 16:36) Resource: Qaṣaṣ al-Anbiyāʾ (Stories of the Prophets) by Ibn Kathīr.

References:
Quran An-Naḥl 16:36; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The prophets are brothers; their religion is one)

overview.heading: Belief in the Last Day (Al-Yawm al-Ākhir)
overview.content:
To believe in everything that will occur after death: the trial of the grave, the Resurrection, the Reckoning, the Scale, the Bridge (Ṣirāṭ), Paradise, and Hellfire. Key "And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are maintaining their prayers." (Al-Anʿām 6:92) Resource: Kitāb al-Jannah wa al-Nār (Book of Paradise and Hell) in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī.

References:
Quran Al-Anʿām 6:92; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent)

overview.heading: Belief in Divine Decree (Al-Qaḍāʾ wal-Qadar)
overview.content:
To believe that Allāh has preordained all things with His prior knowledge and wisdom. This encompasses belief in His all-encompassing knowledge, His recording of all decrees, His will, and His creation of everything. Key "Indeed, all things We created with predestination." (Al-Qamar 54:49) Resource: Sharḥ al-ʿAqīdah al-Ṭaḥāwiyyah by Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz al-Ḥanafī.

References:
Quran Al-Qamar 54:49; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (Allah wrote the decrees of creation before creating the heavens and the earth)

title: The Pillars: The Five Pillars
summary: The Pillars of Islam (Arkān al-Islām) are the fundamental acts of worship that constitute the foundation of a Muslim's faith and practice.

overview.heading: Shahādah (The Testimony of Faith)
overview.content:
Sincere declaration and belief that "Lā ilāha illallāh, Muhammadur Rasūlullāh." Quranic "Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge   [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice." (Ali 'Imran 3:18) Hadith The Prophet ﷺ said, "Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise." (Sahih Muslim 26)

References:
Quran Āl ʿImrān 3:18; Hadith: Sahih Muslim 26 (Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise)

overview.heading: Ṣalāh (The Prayer)
overview.content:
Performing the five obligatory prayers daily at their prescribed times. Quranic "Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times." (An Nisa' 4:103) Hadith The Prophet ﷺ said, "Between a man and shirk and kufr is the abandonment of prayer." (Sahih Muslim 82)

References:
Quran An-Nisāʾ 4:103; Hadith: Sahih Muslim 82 (Between a man and shirk is abandoning prayer)

overview.heading: Zakāh (Obligatory Almsgiving)
overview.content:
Purifying wealth by giving 2.5% of saved wealth annually to specified recipients. Quranic "Take, [O, Muhammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase." (At Tawbah 9:103) Hadith The Prophet ﷺ said, "Islam is built upon five...," including zakah.

References:
Quran At-Tawbah 9:103; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Islam is built on five)

overview.heading: Ṣawm (Fasting Ramadan)
overview.content:
Abstaining from food, drink, and marital relations from dawn to sunset during Ramadan. Quranic "O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous." (Al Baqarah 2:183) Hadith Included in the five pillar hadith.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:183; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Islam is built on five)

overview.heading: Hajj (Pilgrimage to Makkah)
overview.content:
Performing pilgrimage to the Ka'bah once in a lifetime if able. Quranic "And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House   for whoever is able to find thereto a way." (Ali 'Imran 3:97) Hadith Included in the five pillar hadith.

References:
Quran Āl ʿImrān 3:97; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Islam is built on five)

title: The Quran: Final Revelation and Living Guidance
summary: The Qur’an is the eternal, literal Speech of Allah (ﷲ), revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the Angel Jibrīl (Gabriel).

overview.heading: The Quran is Allah’s Final Revelation
overview.content:
The Quran provides guidance for all aspects of life. Believers are encouraged to read, reflect, and act upon its teachings to align their hearts and actions with divine wisdom.

References:
Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:48; Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:3; Quran Al-Ḥijr 15:9; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (The best speech is the Book of Allah)

overview.heading: The Quran Guides Humanity
overview.content:
Through clear instructions, moral teachings, and stories of past nations, the Quran teaches lessons that foster faith, patience, justice, and ethical conduct for spiritual and worldly success.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:2; Quran Al-Isrāʾ 17:9; Quran Ibrāhīm 14:1; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Convey from me, even if one verse)

overview.heading: The Quran Clarifies Belief
overview.content:
It explains the core principles of Tawhid, prophecy, and the Hereafter, strengthening faith and helping believers understand the purpose of life and the path to pleasing Allah.

References:
Quran Al-Anʿām 6:19; Quran An-Naḥl 16:89; Quran Az-Zumar 39:28; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (I left among you the Book of Allah; hold to it and you will not go astray)

overview.heading: The Quran is a Source of Mercy
overview.content:
Reading and reflecting on the Quran brings peace, guidance, and comfort. It reminds believers of Allah’s mercy, encouraging hope, gratitude, and reliance upon Him in all circumstances.

References:
Quran Al-Isrāʾ 17:82; Quran Yūnus 10:57; Quran Al-Aʿrāf 7:52; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (People who gather to recite the Book of Allah are covered by mercy)

overview.heading: The Quran Requires Reflection
overview.content:
Understanding its meanings strengthens belief. Believers are urged to ponder verses, seek knowledge, and apply lessons practically, transforming reading into action and guidance into daily living.

References:
Quran Muḥammad 47:24; Quran Ṣād 38:29; Quran An-Nisāʾ 4:82; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The one proficient in the Quran is with the noble, righteous scribes)

overview.heading: Recitation Elevates the Heart
overview.content:
Reciting the Quran aloud with focus and reverence nourishes the soul, instills tranquility, and enhances spiritual connection with Allah, making worship more heartfelt and intentional.

References:
Quran Al-Muzzammil 73:4; Quran Al-Isrāʾ 17:106; Quran Az-Zumar 39:23; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Beautify the Quran with your voices)

overview.heading: The Quran Guides Morality
overview.content:
It teaches ethics, justice, and compassion. Applying these principles in personal conduct fosters integrity, humility, and a harmonious life aligned with divine expectations.

References:
Quran An-Naḥl 16:90; Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:8; Quran Al-Aʿrāf 7:199; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (His character was the Quran)

overview.heading: The Quran Encourages Knowledge
overview.content:
Believers are instructed to seek understanding, reflect, and learn. Knowledge nurtures wisdom, strengthens conviction, and enables proper application of divine guidance in all aspects of life.

References:
Quran Ṭā Hā 20:114; Quran Az-Zumar 39:9; Quran Al-Mujādilah 58:11; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it)

overview.heading: The Quran Protects from Misguidance
overview.content:
Following its teachings shields believers from false beliefs, moral corruption, and spiritual deviation. Its guidance creates a firm foundation for ethical living and trust in Allah’s commands.

References:
Quran Al-Anʿām 6:155; Quran Al-Baqarah 2:185; Quran Al-Aʿrāf 7:3; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (The devil flees a house where Surah Al-Baqarah is recited)

overview.heading: The Quran Promotes Justice
overview.content:
It emphasizes fairness, honesty, and equality. Implementing these principles in daily life nurtures ethical behavior, protects rights, and establishes social harmony in accordance with divine instruction.

References:
Quran An-Nisāʾ 4:58; Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:8; Quran Al-Ḥadīd 57:25; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection)

overview.heading: The Quran Encourages Patience
overview.content:
Its stories and guidance teach resilience in adversity. Reflecting on divine wisdom strengthens perseverance, hope, and trust in Allah’s plan, fostering spiritual growth and emotional balance.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:153; Quran Āl ʿImrān 3:200; Quran Az-Zumar 39:10; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (Amazing is the affair of the believer; if harmed, he is patient)

overview.heading: The Quran Strengthens Faith
overview.content:
Regular study and reflection deepen Iman. Understanding its wisdom and applying lessons encourages moral behavior, ethical decisions, and a heart aligned with Allah’s guidance.

References:
Quran Al-Aḥzāb 33:34; Quran Al-Anfāl 8:2; Quran Al-Fatḥ 48:4; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Faith has more than seventy branches)

overview.heading: The Quran Encourages Worship
overview.content:
It calls believers to prayer, remembrance, and righteous deeds. Following its commands transforms spiritual devotion into everyday actions, connecting the heart and life to Allah’s pleasure.

References:
Quran Al-ʿAnkabūt 29:45; Quran Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56; Quran Ṭā Hā 20:14; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (Between a man and shirk is abandoning prayer)

overview.heading: The Quran is a Source of Healing
overview.content:
Its words bring comfort, guidance, and reassurance. Reflecting and acting upon them nurtures mental, emotional, and spiritual well being while strengthening reliance on Allah’s wisdom.

References:
Quran Al-Isrāʾ 17:82; Quran Yūnus 10:57; Quran Fuṣṣilat 41:44; Hadith: Sahih Bukhari (Al-Fatihah was used as ruqyah and approved by the Prophet)

overview.heading: The Quran Must Be Applied
overview.content:
Understanding alone is insufficient; believers must implement its guidance in daily life. Action transforms knowledge into practice, faith into ethics, and devotion into tangible obedience.

References:
Quran Al-Ḥashr 59:18; Quran Al-Baqarah 2:44; Quran Aṣ-Ṣaff 61:2-3; Hadith: Sahih Muslim (The Quran is proof for you or against you)

title: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (Life and Legacy)
summary: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the final Messenger of Allah, sent as a mercy to all worlds (*Al-Anbiya 21:107*). His life (Seerah) embodies the Qur'an and provides the best example (Uswatun Hasanah) of faith, character, and leadership for believers (Al-Ahzab 33:21).

overview.heading: Final Prophet Sent to All Humanity
overview.content:
Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, and his message is for all people. The Qur'an also records that the jinn heard the message, underscoring its universality.

References:
Quran Al-Aḥzāb 33:40; Quran Al-Aʿrāf 7:158; Quran Al-Jinn 72:1; Seerah: Ar-Raheeq al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar)

overview.heading: First Revelation in the Cave of Hira
overview.content:
The first revelation came through Jibril with the command "Read" (Iqra), marking the beginning of prophethood, traditionally dated to 610 CE when he was about forty.

References:
Hadith: Sahih al-Bukhari 4953; Seerah: The Life of the Prophet by Ibn Kathir (abridged)

overview.heading: Preached Tawhid in Makkah for 13 Years
overview.content:
He called people to worship Allah alone for about thirteen years in Makkah, enduring persecution, boycott, and the loss of close supporters.

References:
Quran Al-Ḥijr 15:94; Seerah: Sirat Ibn Hisham

overview.heading: Hijrah to Madinah - Turning Point
overview.content:
The migration (Hijrah) in 622 CE marked a decisive turning point and later became the starting point of the Islamic calendar.

References:
Quran An-Naḥl 16:110; Seerah: When the Moon Split by Safiur Rahman al-Mubarakpuri

overview.heading: Established the Islamic State in Madinah
overview.content:
He built the Masjid, established brotherhood (mu'akhah) between the Muhajirun and Ansar, and enacted the Constitution of Madinah.

References:
Seerah: Constitution of Madinah; Madinan Society at the Time of the Prophet by Akram Diya al-Umari

overview.heading: Defensive Battles by Divine Permission
overview.content:
After permission to fight was granted to those wronged, battles such as Badr, Uhud, and the Trench were fought in defense against aggression.

References:
Quran Al-Ḥajj 22:39; Quran Al-Baqarah 2:190; Seerah: The Noble Life of the Prophet by Ali Muhammad as-Sallabi

overview.heading: Conquest of Makkah with Mercy
overview.content:
In 8 AH he entered Makkah and granted a general amnesty, emphasizing mercy over vengeance.

References:
Seerah: Conquest of Makkah accounts in major seerah works

overview.heading: Farewell Sermon and Completion of the Religion
overview.content:
During the Farewell Pilgrimage, he emphasized rights, equality, and accountability, and the verse announcing the perfection of the religion was revealed.

References:
Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:3; Seerah: Farewell Pilgrimage accounts in hadith and seerah works

overview.heading: Passed Away in Madinah
overview.content:
He passed away in 11 AH (632 CE) in the home of Aisha (RA) after completing his mission, leaving the Qur'an and Sunnah as the community's guidance.

References:
Hadith: Sahih al-Bukhari 4440; Seerah: accounts of his passing in Madinah

overview.heading: His Character Was the Living Qur'an
overview.content:
Aisha (RA) described his character as the Qur'an itself, reflecting truthfulness, trustworthiness, mercy, patience, humility, and justice.

References:
Hadith: Sahih Muslim 746a; Quran Al-Qalam 68:4; Shama'il al-Muhammadiyyah by al-Tirmidhi

title: The Prayer: (Salat)
summary: Prayer is the reset that brings your body, heart, and discipline back into harmony with Allah.

overview.heading: Prayer Connects to Allah
overview.content:
Salah is the link between the believer and Allah, nurturing spiritual awareness, mindfulness, and consistent reflection on divine guidance throughout life.

References:
Quran Al-ʿAnkabūt 29:45

overview.heading: Five Daily Prayers
overview.content:
Observing the five daily prayers structures time, reinforces discipline, and creates regular opportunities for remembrance, reflection, and connection with Allah.

References:
Quran Hūd 11:114

overview.heading: Prayer Requires Purity
overview.content:
Wudu and cleanliness before prayer prepare the body and heart. Physical purification mirrors spiritual readiness, enhancing focus, sincerity, and connection during worship.

References:
Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:6

overview.heading: Concentration Strengthens Prayer
overview.content:
Focus (khushu) deepens spiritual connection, increases devotion, and ensures that salah becomes a mindful act rather than a routine ritual.

References:
Quran Al-Muʾminūn 23:1-2

overview.heading: Supplication Complements Prayer
overview.content:
Dua within or after salah expresses dependence, gratitude, and humility. It reinforces connection with Allah and the sincerity of worship.

References:
Hadith: Sahih Muslim 2724

overview.heading: Prayer Brings Tranquility
overview.content:
Regular salah calms the heart, reduces stress, and strengthens faith. It instills patience and gratitude, providing spiritual balance throughout daily life.

References:
Quran Ṭā Hā 20:14

overview.heading: Consistency is Key
overview.content:
Performing prayers consistently fosters discipline, strengthens routine worship, and reinforces connection with Allah regardless of circumstances or personal challenges.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:238

overview.heading: Prayer Elevates Character
overview.content:
Salah instills patience, humility, and self discipline. Its regular practice shapes moral behavior, ethical conduct, and spiritual growth in everyday life.

References:
Quran Al-ʿAnkabūt 29:45

overview.heading: Prayer as Reminder
overview.content:
Each salah reminds believers of accountability, purpose, and divine mercy. Reflection during prayer strengthens awareness and directs choices toward ethical and spiritual growth.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:238

overview.heading: Facing Challenges with Prayer
overview.content:
Regular prayer nurtures resilience and reliance on Allah. During trials, believers find strength, patience, and clarity through mindful worship.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:45

overview.heading: Prayer Inspires Gratitude
overview.content:
Reflection during salah reinforces appreciation for Allah’s blessings. Gratitude expressed through prayer nurtures contentment, humility, and ethical behavior.

References:
Quran Ibrāhīm 14:7

overview.heading: Prayer Strengthens Community
overview.content:
Congregational prayers build unity, social bonds, and collective accountability. Observing salah in community nurtures compassion, empathy, and shared devotion.

References:
Quran At-Tawbah 9:71

overview.heading: Salah Enhances Reflection
overview.content:
Moments of worship offer time to contemplate life, purpose, and Allah’s guidance. Reflection strengthens faith, moral awareness, and intentional living.

References:
Quran Al-Muʾminūn 23:1-2

overview.heading: Intentions Matter
overview.content:
Prayers are accepted when performed with sincerity. Mindful intentions ensure actions are meaningful, spiritually rewarding, and aligned with divine guidance.

References:
Hadith: Sahih Bukhari 1

overview.heading: Prayer Nourishes the Heart
overview.content:
Salah refreshes the soul, strengthens spiritual resilience, and nurtures emotional balance. Regular engagement fosters closeness to Allah and inner peace.

References:
Quran Ar-Rūm 30:17-18

title: Duʿāʾ and Dhikr
summary: Duʿāʾ (supplication) and Dhikr (remembrance) are the core of worship and the direct connection between the servant and Allah. They are the most beloved acts to Allah and the means to attain His mercy, blessings, and protection.

overview.heading: Duʿāʾ is the Essence of Worship
overview.content:
Supplication is an act of worship that demonstrates the servant's utter dependence upon and need for Allah.

References:
'Your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you...' (Ghāfir 40:60) Resource: Al-Duʿāʾ by Imam At-Ṭabarānī.

overview.heading: Dhikr Revives the Heart & Earns Rewards
overview.content:
Remembering Allah frequently with the tongue and heart removes heedlessness, brings tranquility, and earns immense rewards.

References:
'Those who believe and whose hearts find peace in the remembrance of Allah. Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find peace.' (Ar-Raʿd 13:28) Resource: Al-Kalim aṭ-Ṭayyib by Ibn Taymiyyah.

overview.heading: Duʿāʾ is Accepted in Three Ways
overview.content:
Allah either grants what you asked, averts an equivalent harm, or stores its reward for the Hereafter.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'No Muslim supplicates with a duʿāʾ that does not involve sin or severing kinship, but Allah gives him one of three things: He either answers it quickly, stores it for him in the Hereafter, or averts an equivalent evil from him.' (Musnad Aḥmad 11133 - Ṣaḥīḥ) Resource: Fatḥ al-Bārī (Commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī) by Ibn Ḥajar.

overview.heading: Best Times for Duʿāʾ Include Sujūd & Last Third of Night
overview.content:
Certain times and situations are most conducive for acceptance, such as during prostration, between Adhān and Iqāmah, and while traveling.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration, so increase supplication (then).' (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 482) Resource: Al-Adhkār by Imam An-Nawawī (Chapter on Times for Duʿāʾ).

overview.heading: Key Daily Adhkār are Prescribed for Morning & Evening
overview.content:
Specific, verified remembrances protect the believer, earn thousands of rewards, and are a fortress against Shayṭān.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever says in the morning and evening: Ḥasbunallāhu wa niʿmal-Wakīl (Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs) seven times, Allah will suffice him for what concerns him.' (Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5081 - Ḥasan) Resource: Ḥiṣn al-Muslim (Fortress of the Muslim) by Dr. Saʿīd al-Qaḥṭānī.

overview.heading: Begin with Allah's Praise & Ṣalāh upon the Prophet ﷺ
overview.content:
The proper etiquette of duʿāʾ includes starting by praising Allah and sending blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ heard a man supplicating without praising Allah or sending Ṣalāh upon him, so he said: 'This man rushed.' Then he taught: 'When one of you supplicates, let him begin by praising Allah and glorifying Him, then send Ṣalāh upon the Prophet ﷺ, then supplicate as he wishes.' (Sunan At-Tirmidhi 3477 - Ḥasan) Resource: ʿUddat as-Ṣābirīn by Ibn al-Qayyim.

overview.heading: Duʿāʾ Requires Sincerity, Certainty, & Avoiding Haram Sustenance
overview.content:
For duʿāʾ to be accepted, one must have a sincere heart, be certain of the response, and ensure their food, drink, and clothing are lawful.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ mentioned a disheveled traveler raising his hands to the sky saying 'O Lord, O Lord!' while his food, drink, and clothing were from Ḥarām sources, 'So how can his duʿāʾ be answered?' (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1015) Resource: Al-Duʿāʾ wa Atharuhu fī Dafʿ al-Balāʾ by Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī.

overview.heading: Primary Sources (Qur'an & Hadith)
overview.content:
Core Qur'anic verses and authenticated narrations that ground duʿāʾ and dhikr practice.

References:
Qur'anic Verses Cited: Al-Baqarah 2:152 - 'Remember Me; I will remember you.'; Al-Baqarah 2:201 - 'Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good...'; Al-Baqarah 2:216 - 'And it may be that you dislike a thing which is good for you...'; Ar-Raʿd 13:28 - 'Those who believe and whose hearts find peace in the remembrance of Allah...'; Ghāfir 40:60 - 'Your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you...'; Al-Ḥujurāt 49:6 - 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate...'. Hadith Collections & References: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6407 (The example of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6340 (The duʿāʾ of any one of you will be answered so long as he is not impatient); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3995 (Facing Qiblah during duʿāʾ); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6110 (On the virtue of dhikr gatherings); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6389 (Most frequent duʿāʾ of the Prophet ﷺ); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3370 (Ṣalāh upon the Prophet ﷺ in Tashahhud); Book of Duʿāʾ (كتاب الدعوات) in Bukhārī; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 483 (Duʿāʾ in sujūd); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 592 (Tasbīḥ after prayer); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1015 (Importance of lawful sustenance for duʿāʾ acceptance); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2732 (Duʿāʾ for others); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 476 ('Rabbana lakal-ḥamd...'); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 482 (Closeness to Allah in sujūd); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 487 ('Subbūḥun Quddūs...' in rukūʿ and sujūd); Book of Dhikr and Duʿāʾ (كتاب الذكر والدعاء) in Muslim; Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5081 (Morning/evening adhkār); Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5088 (Protection duʿāʾ); Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4855 (Warning against gatherings without dhikr); Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1501 (Counting dhikr on fingers); Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1425 (Qunūt duʿāʾ); Sunan Abī Dāwūd 775 (Opening duʿāʾ in prayer); Sunan Ibn Mājah 3871 (Duʿāʾ for ʿĀfiyah); Sunan Ibn Mājah 897 ('Rabbighfir lī' between prostrations); Sunan Ibn Mājah 925 (Various adhkār); Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3372 ('Duʿāʾ is worship'); Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3477 (Etiquettes of duʿāʾ); Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3383 (Best dhikr); Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 2926 (Reward for reciting Qur'an letters); Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3522 (Duʿāʾ for firmness of heart); Musnad Aḥmad 11133 (Three responses to duʿāʾ); Musnad Aḥmad 13964 (Duʿāʾ for intercession); Al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (Ṭabarānī) 6190 ('Duʿāʾ is the weapon of the believer'); Al-Adab al-Mufrad (Bukhārī) - various chapters on etiquettes.

overview.heading: Classical Texts & Commentaries
overview.content:
Core compilations and scholarly commentaries for deeper study of duʿāʾ and dhikr.

References:
Primary Duʿāʾ & Dhikr Collections: Al-Adhkār - Imām Yaḥyā ibn Sharaf al-Nawawī (631-676 AH); Al-Kalim al-Ṭayyib - Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah (661-728 AH); Al-Duʿāʾ - Imām Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī (260-360 AH); Al-Duʿāʾ wa Atharuhu fī Dafʿ al-Balāʾ - Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī (736-795 AH). Hadith Commentaries: Fatḥ al-Bārī - Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī (773-852 AH); Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim - Imām al-Nawawī. Spiritual & Theological Works: ʿUddat al-Ṣābirīn wa Dhakhīrat al-Shākirīn - Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691-751 AH); Madārij al-Sālikīn - Ibn al-Qayyim; Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn - Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī (450-505 AH); Al-Wābil al-Ṣayyib - Ibn al-Qayyim. Specialized Fiqh of Duʿāʾ: Fatāwā al-Duʿāʾ in Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā (Ibn Taymiyyah); Al-Qawl al-Mubīn fī Adab al-Duʿāʾ; Miftāḥ Dār al-Saʿādah - Ibn al-Qayyim.

title: The Heart: Purification & Spiritual Diseases
summary: The heart (qalb) in Islam is the spiritual center of human existence the seat of faith, intention, and moral consciousness. Its purification (tazkiyah) is the ultimate purpose of revelation.

overview.heading: The Heart is the Seat of Faith & Accountability
overview.content:
Allah judges by what is in hearts, not mere outward actions.

References:
"Allah does not look at your appearances or wealth, but at your hearts and deeds." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2564). Resource: Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm ad-Dīn (Revival of Religious Sciences) by Al-Ghazālī Book on Heart Diseases.

overview.heading: Spiritual Diseases Corrupt the Heart
overview.content:
Hypocrisy (nifāq), arrogance (kibr), envy (ḥasad), and heedlessness (ghaflah) are fatal diseases.

References:
"In their hearts is disease, so Allah has increased their disease..." (Al-Baqarah 2:10). Resource: ʿUddat aṣ-Ṣābirīn (Provisions for the Patient) by Ibn al-Qayyim Chapter on Envy.

overview.heading: Purification Requires Knowledge & Action
overview.content:
One must first learn the diseases, then actively combat them through worship and character refinement.

References:
"He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who corrupts it." (Ash-Shams 91:9-10). Resource: Mukhtaṣar Minhāj al-Qāṣidīn (Abridgement of The Path of the Seekers) by Ibn Qudāmah.

overview.heading: Arrogance (Kibr) is Rejecting Truth & Despising People
overview.content:
The root of Iblīs’s sin, it prevents entry to Paradise.

References:
"Whoever has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will not enter Paradise." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 91). Resource: Kitāb al-Kabāʾir (The Major Sins) by Adh-Dhahabī Chapter on Arrogance.

overview.heading: Envy (Ḥasad) Consumes Good Deeds
overview.content:
It means wishing for Allah’s blessings to be removed from others.

References:
"Beware of envy, for it consumes good deeds as fire consumes wood." (Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4903 Ḥasan). Resource: Al-Fawāʾid (Points of Benefit) by Ibn al-Qayyim Section on Heart Maladies.

overview.heading: Showing Off (Riyāʾ) Nullifies Worship
overview.content:
Seeking praise for worship instead of Allah’s pleasure.

References:
"The slightest amount of showing off is shirk (polytheism)." (Sunan Ibn Mājah 3989 Ṣaḥīḥ). Resource: Kashf al-Khafāʾ (Unveiling the Hidden) by Al-ʿAjlūnī Entry on Riyāʾ.

overview.heading: Love of the World is the Root of All Faults
overview.content:
Excessive attachment to dunyā weakens the heart’s connection to Allah.

References:
"The love of this world is the root of every sin." (Al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ 6066 Ḥasan). Resource: Al-Zuhd (Asceticism) by Imām Aḥmad Collection on Detachment.

overview.heading: Cures Include: Repentance, Dhikr, Qur’an, Good Company
overview.content:
Specific remedies for each disease from Prophetic guidance.

References:
"Hearts rust as iron rusts. Their polish is the remembrance (dhikr) of Allah." (Shuʿab al-Īmān 1596 Ḥasan). Resource: Al-Wābil aṣ-Ṣayyib (The Gentle Rain) by Ibn al-Qayyim On Dhikr’s Effects.

overview.heading: The Sound Heart is Free from Shirk, Hatred & Envy
overview.content:
It submits solely to Allah and wishes good for all Muslims.

References:
"The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 10). Resource: Madārij as-Sālikīn (Stations of the Seekers) by Ibn al-Qayyim Grades of Heart Soundness.

overview.heading: Constant Self-Accounting (Muḥāsabah) is Necessary
overview.content:
Regularly checking one’s intentions and actions.

References:
Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "Hold yourselves accountable before you are held accountable." (Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ 1/52). Resource: Al-Ḥisbah fī al-Islām (Accountability in Islam) by Ibn Taymiyyah.

title: The Manners: Islamic Etiquette (Adab)
summary: Islamic manners (Adab) are not mere social etiquette but an integral part of faith (Īmān), encompassing how we interact with Allah, His creation, and ourselves.

overview.heading: Good Character Completes Faith
overview.content:
The most beloved to Allah are those with best manners.

References:
"The most perfect believer in faith is he who is best in character." (Sunan at-Tirmidhī 1162 – Ṣaḥīḥ). Resource: Al-Adab al-Mufrad by Imām al-Bukhārī – Comprehensive manners collection.

overview.heading: Begin with Salām (Peace Greeting)
overview.content:
Spreading peace is a means to Paradise and increases love.

References:
"You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I inform you of something which will make you love one another? Spread Salām among yourselves." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 54). Resource: Riyāḍ aṣ-Ṣāliḥīn by Imām al-Nawawī – Chapter on Salām.

overview.heading: Lower Your Voice & Speak Kindly
overview.content:
A believer's speech is always measured, gentle, and truthful.

References:
"And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys." (Luqmān 31:19). Resource: Al-Adhkar by Imām al-Nawawī – Chapter on Speech Manners.

overview.heading: Show Mercy to Earn Allah’s Mercy
overview.content:
Mercy encompasses all creation humans, animals, and the environment.

References:
"Those who are merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in heaven will have mercy upon you." (Sunan at-Tirmidhī 1924 – Ṣaḥīḥ). Resource: Al-Kabā'ir by Adh-Dhahabī – Sections on cruelty.

overview.heading: Practice Modesty in Dress & Gaze
overview.content:
Modesty (ḥayāʾ) is a branch of faith that beautifies conduct.

References:
"Modesty brings nothing but good." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6117). Resource: Ḥijāb al-Mar'ah al-Muslimah by Al-Albānī – On Islamic dress code.

overview.heading: Honor Parents Absolutely
overview.content:
After Allah, parents have the greatest right over a person.

References:
"And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and be kind to parents..." (Al-Isrāʾ 17:23). Resource: Birr al-Wālidayn by Ibn al-Jawzī – Book on honoring parents.

overview.heading: Rights of Neighbors are Sacred
overview.content:
The neighbor's right is so emphasized that the Prophet ﷺ thought they might inherit.

References:
"Jibrīl kept recommending the neighbor to me until I thought he would make him an heir." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6015). Resource: Al-Adab al-Mufrad – Chapters on neighborly rights.

overview.heading: Control Anger & Forgive Others
overview.content:
True strength lies in self-control during anger, not in physical power.

References:
"The strong is not the one who overcomes people by his strength, but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6114). Resource: ʿUddat aṣ-Ṣābirīn by Ibn al-Qayyim – Chapter on Patience.

overview.heading: Honesty in All Transactions
overview.content:
Truthfulness leads to righteousness and Paradise.

References:
"Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6094). Resource: Al-Bayʿ wal-Shirāʾ by Ibn ʿUthaymīn – On business ethics.

overview.heading: Respect for Elders & Kindness to Young
overview.content:
A society is balanced when elders are respected and young are shown mercy.

References:
"He is not of us who does not have mercy on our young nor honor our elders." (Sunan at-Tirmidhī 1919 – Ḥasan). Resource: Al-Ādāb ash-Sharʿiyyah by Ibn Mufliḥ – Comprehensive manners text.

title: The Lifestyle: Halal & Haram
summary: The Islamic lifestyle is built upon the foundational principle of distinguishing between the lawful (Halal) and unlawful (Haram) a divine filter through which Muslims evaluate all actions, consumption, and transactions.

overview.heading: Only Allah Has the Right to Declare Halal or Haram
overview.content:
Humans cannot prohibit what Allah has made lawful, nor permit what He has forbidden. This right belongs exclusively to Allah, as He is the Creator and Legislator.

References:
"Do not say concerning what your tongues falsely describe, 'This is lawful and this is forbidden,' to invent lies against Allah..." (An-Naḥl 16:116) Resource: Al-Ḥalāl wal-Ḥarām fil-Islām by Dr. Yūsuf al-Qaraḍāwī – Chapter on Theological Basis.

overview.heading: The Default State of All Things is Permissibility (Al-Ibāḥah al-Aṣliyyah)
overview.content:
Except where definitive evidence establishes prohibition, everything is permissible. This principle applies to food, drinks, transactions, and worldly matters.

References:
"He has explained to you what He has forbidden for you..." (Al-Anʿām 6:119) Resource: Al-Muṣṭalaḥāt al-Arbaʿah by Ibn ʿUthaymīn – Explanation of "Halal, Haram, Makrūh, Mandūb."

overview.heading: Prohibitions Are Few & Clear; Permissibilities Are Vast
overview.content:
Islam is not a religion of restrictions but of channeling freedom within divine boundaries. The core prohibitions are known and limited.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "What Allah has made lawful in His Book is Halal, and what He has forbidden is Haram, and what He remained silent about is pardoned." (Sunan Ibn Mājah 3367 – Ḥasan) Resource: Al-Ashbāh wan-Naẓāʾir by As-Suyūṭī – Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence.

overview.heading: Haram Includes Both the Substance and Means to It
overview.content:
It is not only forbidden to consume Haram (like alcohol) but also to sell, transport, serve, or benefit from its trade. The means to Haram are also Haram.

References:
"Allah has cursed alcohol, its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer..." (Sunan Abī Dāwūd 3674 – Ṣaḥīḥ) Resource: Al-Qawāʿid al-Fiqhiyyah by As-Saʿdī – Legal maxim: "Whatever leads to Haram is itself Haram."

overview.heading: Lawful Food Must Meet Two Criteria: Permissible Source & Proper Slaughter
overview.content:
Animals must be from Halal species and slaughtered according to Islamic rite (Tasmiyyah - mentioning Allah's name, cutting throat, windpipe, and blood vessels).

References:
"Eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses." (Al-Anʿām 6:118) Resource: Fiqh al-Ṭaʿām wal-Ashribah by ʿAbdullah al-Faqīh – Detailed rulings on food.

overview.heading: All Financial Transactions Are Prohibited Unless Proven Permissible
overview.content:
Unlike general matters, financial dealings require evidence of permissibility due to prevalence of fraud and injustice. The default is prohibition until proven Halal.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "The sale is invalid if accompanied by uncertainty (Gharar)." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1513) Resource: Al-Buyūʿ al-Muḥarramah fil-Islām by Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān – Forbidden transactions.

overview.heading: Major Prohibitions Include: Alcohol, Pork, Carnivorous Animals, Blood, Idolatry, Riba (Interest), Gambling, Fortune-Telling, Adultery, & Usurpation
overview.content:
These are explicitly forbidden in the Qur'an and Hadith and have severe spiritual, health, and social consequences.

References:
"He has only forbidden you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah." (Al-Baqarah 2:173) Resource: Al-Kabāʾir by Adh-Dhahabī – The Major Sins.

overview.heading: Necessity (Ḍarūrah) Permits the Prohibited Within Strict Limits
overview.content:
In genuine, life-threatening necessity, prohibited things become temporarily permissible, but only to the extent needed to remove the necessity.

References:
"But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin – then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." (Al-Māʾidah 5:3) Resource: Qawāʿid al-Aḥkām by Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd as-Salām – Rules of necessity.

overview.heading: Doubtful Matters Should Be Avoided to Protect One's Faith & Honor
overview.content:
When uncertain, the pious approach is to leave what causes doubt for what causes no doubt. This safeguards one's religion and conscience.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt." (Sunan at-Tirmidhī 2518 – Ṣaḥīḥ) Resource: Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn by Ibn al-Qayyim – Chapter on precaution.

overview.heading: Haram Consumption Affects Worship & Duʿāʾ Acceptance
overview.content:
Consuming unlawful food, drink, or wealth prevents one's worship from being accepted and blocks the response to supplications.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1015) Resource: Al-Duʿāʾ by Ibn Abī Dunyā – Conditions for acceptance.

title: Family & Marriage: Continuous Growth
summary: The family is the cornerstone of Islamic society, and marriage (nikāḥ) is a sacred covenant (mīthāq ghalīẓ) ordained by Allah for spiritual growth, emotional fulfillment, and the establishment of righteous generations.

overview.heading: Marriage is Half of Faith & Completion of Religion
overview.content:
Marriage protects chastity, fulfills natural desires lawfully, and completes one's faith. It is a Prophetic Sunnah strongly recommended for those able.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "O young people! Whoever among you can afford marriage, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards chastity..." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5065) Resource: Ādāb al-Zawāj (Etiquettes of Marriage) by ʿAbdullah al-Jibrīn.

overview.heading: The Spousal Relationship is Based on Mutual Mercy (Rahmah) & Tranquility (Sakīnah)
overview.content:
Allah describes spouses as garments for one another—providing protection, comfort, and covering. The marital bond is meant for psychological and spiritual peace.

References:
"They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them..." (Al-Baqarah 2:187) Resource: The Muslim Family by Dr. Muḥammad Al-Hashimi.

overview.heading: The Husband is the Guardian (Qawwām) Responsible for Provision & Protection
overview.content:
This leadership is based on responsibility, not superiority. The husband must maintain his family with kindness, consultation (shūrā), and fairness.

References:
"Men are in charge of women by what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend from their wealth..." (An-Nisāʾ 4:34) Resource: Qawwāmah: The Framework of Male Guardianship by Dr. Jasser Auda.

overview.heading: The Wife Has the Right to Kind Treatment, Financial Support, & Intimate Companionship
overview.content:
Her rights are sacred and detailed in the Qur'an and Sunnah. Discharging them is an act of worship for the husband.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "The best of you is he who is best to his wife, and I am the best of you to my wives." (Sunan Ibn Mājah 1977 – Ṣaḥīḥ) Resource: Huqūq al-Zawjayn (Rights of Spouses) by Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān.

overview.heading: Choosing a Spouse Should Prioritize Piety (Dīn) & Good Character
overview.content:
Wealth, beauty, and lineage are secondary considerations. A righteous spouse is the key to a blessed home and successful upbringing of children.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "A woman is married for four things: her wealth, lineage, beauty, and religion. Choose the religious woman, lest your hands be rubbed with dust!" (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5090) Resource: Al-Akhṭāʾ al-Shāʾiʿah fī Ṭalab al-Zawj (Common Mistakes in Seeking Marriage) by ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Nāṣir.

overview.heading: Children Are a Trust (Amānah) & Must Be Raised With Love, Islamic Education, & Good Example
overview.content:
Parents will be held accountable for their upbringing. The first words a child should hear are the call to prayer (adhān) in their ears.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Every one of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock..." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 893) Resource: Tarbiyat al-Awlād fī al-Islām (Raising Children in Islam) by Dr. ʿAbdullah Nāṣiḥ ʿUlwān.

overview.heading: Maintaining Kinship Ties (Ṣilat al-Raḥim) is Obligatory & Brings Blessings
overview.content:
This includes parents, siblings, and extended family. Severing ties is a major sin that brings Allah's curse and withholds blessings.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him maintain the bonds of kinship." (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6138) Resource: Birr al-Wālidayn wa Ṣilat al-Arḥām by Ibn al-Jawzī.

overview.heading: Conflict Resolution Follows the Sequence: Private Advice → Mediation → Arbitration
overview.content:
Disputes should be resolved with wisdom, patience, and seeking intervention from righteous family members if needed.

References:
"If you fear a breach between them, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family..." (An-Nisāʾ 4:35) Resource: Al-Iṣlāḥ bayn al-Zawjayn (Reconciliation Between Spouses) by Dr. Ṣāliḥ al-Ghāmidī.

overview.heading: Divorce is Permitted But the Most Hated Permissible Act to Allah
overview.content:
It is a last resort after all reconciliation efforts fail. The procedure must follow Islamic guidelines to minimize harm.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "The most hateful permissible thing to Allah is divorce." (Sunan Abī Dāwūd 2178 – Ḥasan) Resource: Aḥkām al-Ṭalāq (Rulings of Divorce) by Ibn ʿUthaymīn.

overview.heading: The Family Home Should Be a Place of Remembrance (Dhikr), Prayer, & Mercy
overview.content:
Angels enter homes where Allah is remembered and blessings descend. The home should be a sanctuary from worldly fitnah.

References:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "The example of a home in which Allah is remembered and a home in which Allah is not remembered is like the living and the dead." (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 779) Resource: Kayfa Takūn Usrah Saʿīdah (How to Have a Happy Family) by Dr. ʿĀʾid al-Qarnī.

title: The Community: Building Ummah, Support, and Uplift
summary: Islam thrives in community; this chapter explores solidarity, hospitality, and shared purpose.

overview.heading: Community Strengthens Faith
overview.content:
Engaging in a righteous community fosters support, accountability, and shared worship. Collective action strengthens faith and promotes ethical behavior among members.

References:
Quran Āl ʿImrān 3:104

overview.heading: Supporting One Another
overview.content:
Mutual assistance in times of need nurtures compassion, unity, and social responsibility while reflecting divine guidance in action.

References:
Quran Al-Māʾidah 5:2

overview.heading: Justice in Society
overview.content:
Fair treatment of all community members ensures harmony, prevents conflict, and aligns society with Allah’s principles.

References:
Quran An-Nisāʾ 4:58

overview.heading: Inclusivity and Brotherhood
overview.content:
Welcoming diversity and fostering equality strengthens social bonds. Unity and brotherhood reflect ethical conduct and divine guidance.

References:
Quran Al-Ḥujurāt 49:13

overview.heading: Resolving Conflicts Peacefully
overview.content:
Encouraging dialogue and reconciliation maintains harmony, prevents injustice, and strengthens communal trust in accordance with Islamic principles.

References:
Quran Al-Ḥujurāt 49:9

overview.heading: Collective Worship
overview.content:
Praying, fasting, and performing acts of charity together nurtures unity, strengthens faith, and fosters shared responsibility.

References:
Quran At-Tawbah 9:71

overview.heading: Charity Strengthens Community
overview.content:
Giving zakat and sadaqah supports the needy, reduces inequality, and enhances social cohesion, reflecting ethical and spiritual responsibility.

References:
Quran Al-Baqarah 2:177

overview.heading: Mentorship and Education
overview.content:
Sharing knowledge and guidance empowers individuals, fosters ethical development, and strengthens community resilience and faith.

References:
Hadith: Sahih Muslim 2699

overview.heading: Respecting Leaders
overview.content:
Honoring just leadership nurtures stability, accountability, and obedience to ethical principles while ensuring communal well being.

References:
Quran An-Nisāʾ 4:59
